newsitem.title: CHINA: China begins probe of collectively held assets.
newsitem.headline: China begins probe of collectively held assets.

text.p: China has begun a campaign to inspect the assets and capital stock of urban collectives, the China Securities said on Tuesday.
It said all companies, economic entities, credit cooperatives and retail outlets under urban collectives -- including joint ventures -- would be covered in the inspection.
"The collectively owned economy is an important part of China's public ownership system and has made a great contribution to the country's reform," said the official Xinhua news agency.
"However, problems and contradictions like waste and loss of assets have cropped up in the process of the reform and opening up," it said.
A small-scale assessment of collectively held assets had been under way since July, covering 17,087 enterprises, the agency said. It described that probe as experimental.
China has been concerned about the loss of state assets, and it announced last week the completion of a national registration of state property to curb such losses.
The registration revealed that many state companies had not registered all of their assets and that others had lent or leased them out "in an uncontrolled way", it said.
Ownership of assets was ill-defined in the first three decades following the communist revolution.

But economic reforms launched in 1979, particularly the introduction of public ownership through the sale of shares, has made it necessary to determine what belongs to the state as well as to the collective and private sectors.
